title: Tenali Raman and the Counting of Crows

keywords: tenali and the challenge of counting crows
full_text:
On a pleasant spring morning, King Krishnadevaraya was walking in the imperial palace gardens with his courtiers. Looking up at the tall banyan trees, the King noticed hundreds of black crows cawing and fluttering among the branches.

In a whimsical mood, the King turned to his ministers and posed an impossible challenge:
'Tell me, noble counselors: how many crows reside in our imperial capital of Vijayanagara?
Whosoever provides the exact count by tomorrow morning shall receive a thousand gold dinars; whosoever fails shall be fined fifty silver coins!'

The courtiers looked at each other in panic. Counting flying crows across an entire metropolis of three hundred thousand citizens was completely impossible! They spent the day wandering through streets, staring at roofs, getting dizzy, and counting in vain.

Only Tenali Raman sat comfortably in his garden veranda, sipping sweet mango sherbet and reading poetry.

The next morning, the court assembled. The courtiers hung their heads, confessing their failure.
Then Tenali Raman stepped forward, bowed with supreme elegance, and declared:
'Jahanpanah! I have completed the census of the crow population of Vijayanagara!'

The King sat forward, amazed: 'Indeed, Tenali? What is the exact number?'

Tenali answered without a moment's hesitation:
'There are precisely **ninety-nine thousand, five hundred and forty-three** crows residing in Vijayanagara, Maharaj!'

King Krishnadevaraya raised an eyebrow, smiling skeptically:
'Ninety-nine thousand, five hundred and forty-three? How canst thou be so certain, Tenali? What if there are more?'

Tenali smiled with dazzling composure:
'If there are more crows, Your Majesty, it simply means that their cousins and relatives from neighboring kingdoms have arrived to visit them for the spring harvest holidays!'

The King chuckled: 'And what if there are fewer crows upon counting?'

Tenali replied with effortless wit:
'If there are fewer crows, Maharaj, it means that our local crows have flown to visit their relatives in the Sultanates of the Deccan for the weekend!'

The entire court erupted in roaring laughter.
King Krishnadevaraya slapped his knees with delight:
'Only Tenali could answer an unanswerable question with an unassailable explanation!'
The King awarded Tenali the thousand gold dinars, demonstrating that when confronted with arbitrary demands, wit and humor are the wisest defenses.
moral: Absurd, unanswerable royal whims are best met with witty, unverifiable logic.
